items.title: SageMaker instance preference lists for capacity-aware training
items.why_now: SageMaker Training and Processing Jobs can now take an ordered list of up to five acceptable instance configurations and automatically launch on the first one with available capacity, replacing manual retry loops during GPU shortages.
items.test_plan: Choose one non-production training or processing job that already runs on at least two compatible accelerated instance families. Submit a three-entry preference list with equivalent effective throughput targets, a bounded MaxPendingTimeInSeconds, and the same pinned container/data/seed. Compare queue time, wall-clock time, result quality and total cost against the single-instance baseline.
success_criteria: Median job-start delay falls materially without manual resubmission
Fallback hardware preserves result quality within the workload's defined tolerance
Container, drivers and distributed-training assumptions work on every listed instance type
Fallback cost remains inside an explicit per-job budget
risks: SageMaker does not validate cross-instance GPU architecture, EFA or driver compatibility
Raw FLOPS equivalence does not guarantee equal training time or convergence
Automatic fallback can silently choose a more expensive topology if budgets are not enforced
items.maturity: trial cloud scheduling primitive with primary implementation guidance; workload-specific economics must be measured

items.title: Authority-boundary suite for agent instruction hierarchy
items.why_now: Microsoft AI's draft Chain of Command makes a concrete, testable distinction between authoritative instructions and untrusted content from tools, files, web pages and other AI systems.
items.test_plan: Build 10-20 adversarial fixtures across web pages, retrieved documents, files, tool outputs and delegated subagents. For each fixture, attempt to override a system/policy rule, operator policy, user goal or explicit stop/cancel instruction using lower-authority content.
success_criteria: Untrusted content cannot elevate its own instruction authority
Tool/RAG/file content cannot override higher-priority policy or operator constraints
Every authority delegation is explicit, scoped and auditable
Stop/cancel requests override continued task optimization
risks: Microsoft's code is a design target rather than proof of current model behavior
Prompt wrappers alone can simulate hierarchy without enforcing it at runtime
Authority checks must also cover non-text side effects and delegated subagents
items.maturity: trial security/evaluation pattern derived from a concrete primary governance specification; cross-vendor behavior still requires testing

items.title: Inference control-plane audit for mutation endpoints
items.why_now: CVE-2026-86793 in SGLang shows that a weight-update endpoint plus optional authentication and executable deserialization can become an unauthenticated RCE path. The due three-day review still found no confirmed patched version in the GitHub Advisory Database.
items.test_plan: Inventory every model/weight/adapter/runtime mutation endpoint in one inference environment; test whether each is reachable outside the management network, enforces authentication independently of startup defaults, and accepts pickle or other executable serialization from network clients.
success_criteria: Zero unauthenticated state-mutation endpoints
Administrative endpoints are unavailable from public/service data-plane networks
No untrusted network bytes reach executable deserialization
Mutation actions are authenticated and auditable
risks: Inventory can miss sidecar or framework-specific admin APIs
Managed providers may hide implementation details
As of the Sep 16 review, the public advisory still did not name a confirmed patched version
items.maturity: experimental security audit pattern grounded in a validated public CVE; upstream remediation boundary remains unclear

review_history.note: Three-day review: GitHub Advisory GHSA-m675-99qc-9233, updated Sep 14, still lists patched versions as unknown. Current SGLang docs still expose the administrative tensor-update endpoint. No upstream remediation statement cleared the evidence threshold, so isolation/authentication remain the actionable controls.

items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Encode-Prefill-Decode disaggregation
items.why_now: NVIDIA has published an implementation and workload guidance for separating multimodal encode from LLM prefill/decode.
items.test_plan: Instrument encode, prefill and decode separately on representative image-heavy VLM traffic; compare aggregated serving versus EPD with identical model, prompts and concurrency.
success_criteria: Material p95 TTFT improvement
Higher goodput at equal or lower cost
No meaningful increase in errors or transfer overhead
risks: Vendor benchmark results may not generalize
Decode-heavy or dense-model workloads may see little benefit

review_history.note: No credible independent production-style reproduction surfaced in the three-day review; vendor measurements remain workload-specific.
Seven-day review: no credible non-NVIDIA production-style reproduction cleared the evidence bar. The architecture remains testable, but published gains are still vendor/workload-specific.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash and alias-migration regression test
items.why_now: DeepSeek's primary release documentation is now in the evidence set and, from 04:00 UTC on Sep 14, requests using the still-valid deepseek-v4-pro ID route to V4.1-Flash at Flash rates. That makes the provider migration itself a production regression boundary even before independent benchmark claims mature.
items.test_plan: Run the same representative 20-50 task suite against pre-migration traces/baseline and current deepseek-v4-pro/deepseek-flash responses where available. Record requested model ID, any resolved model/version metadata, task success, p50/p95 latency, tool/schema errors, tokens and cost per successful task.
success_criteria: No material regression on target task success or tool/schema behavior
Observed cost/latency delta is decision-useful and reproducible
Requested and resolved model identities are logged or otherwise auditable
Migration date is recorded in evaluation provenance
risks: Performance superiority remains a vendor claim without a sufficiently comparable independent end-to-end evaluation
Provider aliases can hide immutable backend versions
A pre-migration baseline may be unavailable unless traces were retained

review_history.note: No new stable primary technical documentation plus comparable independent end-to-end evaluation cleared the decision threshold; secondary/community benchmark claims were not used to upgrade the item.

Primary release documentation and technical-report link were located, and the scheduled deepseek-v4-pro alias migration is now effective. Upgrade is for migration/regression testing, not an endorsement of DeepSeek's benchmark claims; independent comparable evaluation remains outstanding.

Seven-day review: no comparable production-style post-migration evaluation or provider-resolved immutable model telemetry cleared the decision threshold. Keep the alias-migration regression suite active.

items.title: Policy gate for persistent agent-memory writes
items.why_now: MemSentry provides a concrete security model for treating persistent memory writes as privileged state transitions rather than ordinary data writes.
items.test_plan: Place a non-production gate before persistent memory writes and evaluate source trust, semantic risk, access/permission impact and blast radius across a small poisoning test corpus.
success_criteria: Known malicious writes are quarantined/reviewed
Benign memory writes retain acceptable false-positive rate
Every decision has provenance and is auditable
risks: Published evidence is synthetic and not independently replicated
Semantic classifiers may not transfer to domain-specific memory

review_history.note: No independent replication or production evidence surfaced in the three-day review; original synthetic evaluation remains the main evidence.
Seven-day review: no independent replication or production evidence materially upgrades the original synthetic memory-poisoning evidence. Keep the gate experimental.

items.title: Internal agent registry with delegated authority
items.why_now: Payment ecosystems are converging on explicit agent identity and registries, making the pattern directly testable inside enterprise agent systems.
items.test_plan: Register 3-5 internal agents with stable IDs, principal/owner, allowed capabilities, policy version, expiry and revocation; require registry lookup plus external policy check before irreversible actions.
success_criteria: Every irreversible action maps to agent, principal and active delegation
Revoked agents lose access without prompt changes
Credential material stays outside the agent runtime
risks: Registry state does not itself stop prompt injection
Poor lifecycle management can create stale authority

review_history.note: Three-day review found no public KYA specification, SDK/reference implementation or cross-network production pilot. The architecture remains useful as an internal experiment, but interoperability evidence has not advanced.

items.title: Hermetic coding-agent canary for untrusted repositories
items.why_now: The Beltdown disclosure shows that sandboxing model-issued shell commands is insufficient when harness-owned Git or tooling can execute outside the sandbox.
items.test_plan: Open a harmless adversarial repository fixture inside a disposable coding-agent environment and verify that agent, harness, Git, indexers and build tools cannot affect host processes/files, reach credential sockets or bypass controlled network egress.
success_criteria: No host filesystem/process effects
No access to host SSH/cloud credential material
All network egress is mediated and auditable
Artifacts leave only through an explicit export path
risks: One canary cannot cover every IDE/plugin/harness path
Isolation that is strong on one OS may not transfer to another
items.maturity: experimental security validation pattern based on a primary vulnerability disclosure; production coverage depends on harness topology

review_history.note: Three-day review found no new independent evidence or vendor-wide hermetic-runtime validation sufficient to promote the canary. Microsoft's new authority model strengthens the broader need for explicit trust boundaries but does not resolve harness escape risk.

items.title: Cost-per-successful-outcome model benchmark harness
items.why_now: AWS/OpenAI published a reproducible harness that measures task correctness and agent trajectory economics instead of only token price, matching the project's task-success-per-cost evaluation principle.
items.test_plan: Replace the published tasks with 50-100 representative internal tasks, pin prompts and model parameters, define a binary/graded quality gate, and record task success, total turns, latency, tokens, review/rework and cost per passing task.
success_criteria: Model ranking is stable across repeated runs
Task-success/cost differences are large enough to affect routing or model choice
Reasoning settings and provider harnesses are configuration-equivalent for any direct comparison
risks: The published AWS comparison uses non-equivalent reasoning settings for some models
LLM judging can bias correctness unless calibrated against human labels
items.maturity: trial methodology; open-source harness is available but published rankings should not be treated as intrinsic model capability

review_history.note: Three-day review found no new pinned cross-model evidence suitable for a fair ranking. The methodology remains useful, but direct comparisons still require equivalent reasoning settings, harnesses and quality gates.

items.title: Dual-layer production monitoring for agents
items.why_now: AWS published a concrete reference architecture that separates agent outcome quality from infrastructure health, reducing the risk of treating successful API calls as successful agent work.
items.test_plan: Instrument one agent workflow with two independent channels: infrastructure signals such as IAM/throttling/tool/network failures, and outcome signals such as goal success, response correctness and tool-trajectory quality. Inject one failure in each layer separately.
success_criteria: A healthy-infrastructure/bad-outcome incident is detected by the quality layer
A good-plan/broken-infrastructure incident is detected by the operations layer
Both alerts point to distinct remediation paths
risks: LLM-as-judge metrics require calibration
Sampling may miss rare failure modes
Reference architecture is AWS-specific even though the pattern is portable
items.maturity: watch-to-trial reference pattern with available implementation guidance

review_history.note: Three-day review found no new independent production measurement validating the reference pattern. Outcome quality and infrastructure health remain logically distinct and worth testing, but evidence has not advanced enough to upgrade maturity.
